description.narrative:
Increased access to education finance: India has approximately 17% of the worlds unbanked population at 230 million, as per a 2021 World Bank study, and this segment has very limited access to formal credit. Further, as per Redseer , India's overall education market, sized at approximately US$223 billion in Calendar Year 2024 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 11-13% between Calendar Year 2024 and Calendar Year 2029, driven by increasing demand for higher education. Noting this, IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will allow Credila to accelerate lending towards access to education finance, including to the underserved EWS segments and women borrowers. This will support higher education for Indian students and allow more students to acquire relevant skills and secure new jobs.
Beyond the project level outcomes, IFC anticipates that this Project will promote greater competitiveness via replication channels by showcasing the viability of providing financing to underserved EWS segments, including women borrowers.

The investment consists of a US$ denominated senior loan to Credila Financial Services Limited (Credila or the Company). IFC has committed up to US$200 million from its own account and supported mobilization of total financing package of US$750 million to the Company. IFCs investment proceeds will be utilized by Credila for financing students overseas education (for under graduation or master degrees), a majority of IFCs proceeds will be targeted towards providing finance to students from the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and a portion will be earmarked towards on-lending to women borrowers (the Project).
